Environment variables

The platform sets a small, fixed group of environment variables in your app's container. Read this page to know which ones exist, when each is present, and which ones are not set for you.

Always set#

VariableValueUse it for
VMNODES_APP_IDThe app's id, a stringThe audience your app checks in the identity token. @vmnodes/identity reads it.
VMNODES_APP_NAMEThe name you gave the app at launch, such as expensesNaming the entities you share: <VMNODES_APP_NAME>.<thing>.
VMNODES_ENVIRONMENTproduction for an app launched from the portalTelling environments apart.

Set on the hosted platform#

VariableValueUse it for
VMNODES_PORTAL_URLThe portal address the platform gives your app. Read it; never type it inWhere the identity key set is found when VMNODES_ISSUER_URL is not set.
VMNODES_ISSUER_URLThe address that issues identity tokensThe iss value your app requires, and where the key set is fetched: <VMNODES_ISSUER_URL>/auth/jwks.

Your app does not need to set either. If both are missing, new VmnodesIdentity() throws at start-up.

Secrets#

Secrets are placed in the container's environment when a version is deployed. They are never shown in the portal.

VariablePresent whenValue
DATABASE_URLvmnodes.json has ever been deployed with "database": trueA postgres:// connection string. It stays set if you later remove the key.
VMNODES_PUBLISH_TOKENProduction, and publishes in vmnodes.json is non-emptyThe bearer token for the publish calls.
VMNODES_API_URLSame as VMNODES_PUBLISH_TOKENThe address to send those calls to. This one is not secret.

An app with no publishes entry gets no VMNODES_PUBLISH_TOKEN and no VMNODES_API_URL. Reading the value in code gives undefined; write the app so it still starts, as the starter does, and publishes nothing.

If DATABASE_URL is set, your app's container can reach that database. It cannot reach other apps.

Not set#

  • PORT. Your app must listen on port 3000, on all addresses (0.0.0.0). Read process.env.PORT only as a local-testing override with 3000 as the fallback.
  • NODE_ENV, HOST, and every other variable not listed above. Set what you need in your Dockerfile with ENV.

An app must not depend on any variable that is not on this page. Others may exist for the platform's own use and can change.

Build argument#

BUILD_COMMIT is a build argument, not a runtime variable. The platform passes the exact 40-character commit it built as --build-arg BUILD_COMMIT=<sha>. A Dockerfile that wants the value at run time declares ARG BUILD_COMMIT and ENV BUILD_COMMIT=$BUILD_COMMIT, as the starter does. See Build, run and security checks.

Local development#

On your own machine none of these are set. The starter's npm run dev command sets VMNODES_PORTAL_URL and VMNODES_APP_ID (to app_local_dev) and starts a stand-in portal at http://127.0.0.1:4100. See Identity SDK.
